basics.name: Mark Cheli
basics.label: Director, Product Operations & Strategy · Onshape (PTC)
basics.summary: Product and operations leader who still ships code. I run Onshape's Product Operations & Strategy team at PTC: product-led growth, product analytics and the data warehouse, internal AI adoption, localization operations, and the planning cadence the R&D org runs on. Thirteen years at PTC from intern to director, with stops leading engineering teams of 35+ and a 40-person training-products organization. At home I run a 40-container homelab and build the apps on it.

work.name: PTC — Onshape
work.summary: Lead the product-operations and analytics function for Onshape, PTC's SaaS-native CAD platform. Scope spans product-led growth, product analytics and the data warehouse, internal AI adoption, localization operations, the org's planning and review cadence, and hands-on full-stack development on early-stage initiatives.
highlights: Own the product analytics platform: AWS Redshift warehouse, dbt models, Prefect orchestration, Streamlit dashboards and Looker — the data the product, GTM and leadership teams plan against.

Drive internal AI adoption across R&D: agentic-harness guidelines for GitHub Copilot, evaluation of Claude via LiteLLM over AWS Bedrock for 1,000+ users, custom MCP servers for the warehouse and data dictionary, and a proposed budget and governance model for AI developer tools.
Run the product-led growth program: the PLG discovery program and its epics, onboarding and in-app messaging work, signup analytics, and the API rate-limit and quota policy tied to plan tiers.
Run localization operations for an 11-locale product: translation-management vendor selection and renegotiation, XLIFF/TBX pipelines, and a ~1,300-term glossary.
Ship production code when speed beats handoff: internal Flask services connecting Onshape to Salesforce, billing and the warehouse; a Python admin library; internal product and admin portals.
Served as interim Director of Business Operations for the Onshape business unit (Jun–Sep 2022): lead routing, CPQ and executive dashboards.
Hire and manage a small product-ops/analytics team plus developers and interns; own FY planning epics and tech-debt planning for the group.
